title: The record code and the acknowledgement of the search access record, the case-list scope parameters, the page bounds and the screen ID are named in no source
source: Work Package _work/msr/wp/B2-P5-001.md (story line RWB-P5-E1033-APP); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 033 Search across cases v1.md sections 3, 12 and 15; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P5 Document hub v2.md API-P5-009; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P5 Document hub v3.md A2.6
description: The search is a read with six values that no source fixes. (1) The record code the DP-03 library gives an access event of a search, and what the request waits for as the confirmation the legacy story calls a confirmed access-log write; FEAT-ACA-08 puts the access log into the decision log but names no code and no acknowledgement. (2) The query parameter names of the case-list read of rwb-case that return the case IDs in scope with their case numbers; the default ruling gives the case list to P3 and the legacy call is an in-process method signature only. (3) The behaviour of the page parameter above the cap and the exact page bounds of GET /documents beyond the legacy 'size default 50, maximum 50'. (4) The screen ID of the Document search page: screens.txt holds none and the legacy story records the same absence. (5) The key of a decision record whose subject is a search across cases rather than one case. (6) The migration file name and version number of the one DP-15 step that carries the three search indexes, since the legacy file V1_5_033 belongs to the monolith sequence. The story names each of them with the placeholder and builds no value from guesswork.
evidence: TSD P5 v2 API-P5-009 gives the purpose, the request query list, the response DocumentSearchPage and the errors 401, 403, 422, 503, with no page bound and no record code; FSD P5 v3 A2.6 repeats the legacy criteria and names no field of an access record; legacy section 15 states 'screens.txt holds no screen ID for search across cases'; legacy section 13 gives V1_5_033__document_search_indexes.sql in the monolith sequence; context pack P5 gives the service, the schema, the topic and the eleven owned tables but no record code and no migration numbering
proposed: Fix the six values at the wave 1 contract review: the access record code from the DP-03 library code set, the acknowledgement shape, the case-list query parameters, the page bounds, the screen ID in screens.txt and the version number of the step in the rwb-document sequence.

title: The two DP-11 contract reads of the legacy in-process calls are absent from the Work Package dependency rows and DP-08 is not among the patterns
source: Work Package _work/msr/wp/B2-P5-001.md (story line RWB-P5-E1033-APP: H eight rows, C = RWB-P3-E1042-CON and RWB-P3-E1043-CON, I = [], X = [], patterns DP01, DP03, DP06, DP07, DP11, DP15, DP19); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md R5.5 (DP-11 and DP-08 rows) and R5.7 rule 2; legacy RWB-E1-033 section 12 ('Published interfaces called': P3 caseIdsInScope and caseNumbers, P4 mayReadUnmasked)
section: RWB-P5-E1033-APP metadata rows 15 to 18, and sections 1, 3, 10, 12.2, 12.8 and 18
description: The legacy search calls two published interfaces of other modules: CaseDirectory.caseIdsInScope and caseNumbers (P3) and mayReadUnmasked (P4). Under DP-11 both become REST contracts with a fake and a 2 s timeout, so the story consumes the case-list read of rwb-case and the authorise decision of rwb-access and needs a C row for each. The Work Package rows are the two parameters and reference-data contracts only, and DP-08 (guard and authorise) is not in the pattern list, so the dependency map shows no contract for either read. The rows are copied exactly as the Work Package fixes them and the two reads are stated in the story text; the masking decision is the one that cannot be mocked away silently, because AC3 and AC4 turn on it.
evidence: Work Package C row holds RWB-P3-E1042-CON and RWB-P3-E1043-CON only; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-11 'REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout, none (C from the legacy dependency)' and DP-08 'Authorise contract of rwb-access and the guard library, H RWB-PLT-E1037-CON; C RWB-P4-E1037-CON'; delivered sibling stories of the same service cite GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId} and POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise as consumed with the C row absent (RWB-P5-E1016-APP, RWB-P5-E1024-APP)
proposed: Add C RWB-P3-E1018-CON and C RWB-P4-E1037-CON to the dependency map of this story at D1, and state in the Build Sequence that the search is buildable from Day 1 against the two fakes.

title: The FSD keeps the PII access log in the ACE common module while the Work Package applies DP-03 to the same record
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P5 Document hub v3.md ('Existing capability check': Sign-in, access check, audit and PII logging, REUSE, ACE common module); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P4 Access and administration v3.md FEAT-ACA-08 'Write the access log into the decision log'; legacy RWB-E1-033 sections 3, 9 and 17; Work Package _work/msr/wp/B2-P5-001.md patterns DP01, DP03
description: Two current sources put the access record of a search in different places. The P5 FSD reuses the ACE common module for PII logging, as the legacy story does, and the legacy story waits for that module's confirmation (AC9). The P4 FSD's FEAT-ACA-08 puts the access log into the append-only decision log, which DP-03 makes local to the service with the central ledger in rwb-decision. The Work Package applies DP-03, so the story writes the record through the local library and publishes it on rwb.decision-record.v1; the ACE common module stays the edge log of the request itself and is not what AC9 waits for. R-PREC would put the technical and functional specifications above the story, but the two specifications also disagree with each other, so the choice is recorded rather than derived.
evidence: FSD P5 v3 existing-capability table: PII logging REUSE ACE common module; FSD P4 v3 feature row FEAT-ACA-08 'Puts access events into the same append-only log, so access and decisions are queried together'; legacy RWB-E1-033 section 3 'The ACE common module writes access events to the PII access log and confirms each write', section 9 'the access event goes to the PII access log of the ACE common module'; Work Package patterns include DP03 and exclude any PII-log pattern
proposed: Confirm at the wave 1 architecture review that every service writes its own access records on the local decision chain and that the ACE common PII log keeps only the request-level audit; if the ACE log must stay the search record, AC9 reverts to that call and DP-03 keeps only the business decision record.
